headline_en: BMET to hire 70 language trainers at 800 taka per hour; apply now
summary_en: BMET will hire 70 guest language trainers to run language courses at government Technical Training Centres (TTCs) in Portuguese, Spanish, Japanese, Russian, French and Italian, 40 of them for Japanese. Trainers are paid 800 taka per hour, up to 4 hours a day. Applications by post by 11 May 2026; written and oral exams on 15 May 2026 at DTTI, Mirpur.

facts.statement: The Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) runs language courses at the government Technical Training Centres (TTCs) and in 2026 is forming a panel of 70 guest language trainers for Portuguese, Spanish, Japanese, Russian, French and Italian.
Of the 70 BMET guest language trainer posts for TTC language courses: Portuguese 6, Spanish 6, Japanese 40, Russian 6, French 6, Italian 6.

Eligibility for BMET guest language trainers: Portuguese, Spanish, Russian and French require at least a Level B1 pass in a language proficiency test; Japanese requires at least HSC plus JLPT N3 or equivalent; Italian requires at least Level A2. Preference goes to people who lived more than three years in the country concerned or worked more than a year as a language trainer at a reputed institution.
BMET guest language trainers at TTCs are paid an honorarium of 800 taka per hour, payable for at most 4 hours per day.

To apply as a BMET guest language trainer, download the form from the BMET website, send a scanned copy online, and also post the original application with attested copies of all educational and experience certificates; applications in person are not accepted. Deadline 11 May 2026.

Written and oral exams for all languages were set for 10am on 15 May 2026 at the Dhaka Technical Teachers Training Institute (DTTI), Mirpur, Dhaka. Candidates who applied under the earlier notice of 26 March 2026 need not reapply.

headline_en: May Day thoughts: where is the worker in financial inclusion?
summary_en: An opinion piece by banker M M Mahbub Hasan argues that Bangladeshi workers, including migrant workers, are included in finance but not financially empowered. It cites Bangladesh Bank's low-cost 10/50/100 taka 'no-frills' accounts, open also to migrants, and their remittance inflows, and calls for savings, investment, health insurance and reintegration products for migrant families.

facts.statement: About 15 million (1 crore 50 lakh) Bangladeshi migrants work in 176 countries, most of them working people; their yearly remittance is more than 2.5 to 3 lakh crore taka.
facts.source_in_article: M M Mahbub Hasan, banker and development researcher (opinion)

facts.statement: Bangladesh Bank promotes 10, 50 and 100 taka 'no-frills' (nominal-cost) bank accounts, through bank branches, sub-branches, agent outlets and digital channels, to bring farmers, workers, the extreme poor, migrants and marginal groups into formal finance.
facts.source_in_article: M M Mahbub Hasan, banker and development researcher (opinion)

facts.statement: Bangladesh Bank's latest report (October-December 2025): about 2 crore 92 lakh 32 thousand no-frills accounts hold deposits of about 5,116 crore 46 lakh taka; about 827 crore taka of remittance came into these accounts during the review period.
facts.source_in_article: Bangladesh Bank report, cited by the writer

facts.statement: Up to December 2025, from a 750 crore taka refinance fund, about 901 crore taka in low-interest loans was given to 1,02,606 customers for income-generating activities of low-income people.
facts.source_in_article: Bangladesh Bank report, cited by the writer

facts.statement: The writer argues remittance can build wealth with policy support and that savings, investment facilities, health insurance and reintegration-oriented financial products for migrant families after return are urgently needed.
facts.source_in_article: M M Mahbub Hasan, banker and development researcher (opinion)

headline_en: Chief Adviser orders action against forged training certificates to protect labour market reputation
summary_en: On 8 February 2026, Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus, chairing the National Skills Development Authority (NSDA) governing body, ordered action against forgery of skills training certificates, which he said is damaging Bangladeshi workers' reputation abroad. The meeting decided on an integrated skills ecosystem with a common curriculum and standards, approved NSDA long-term goals including recognition of prior learning, and discussed giving CDCs to trainees of the Institutes of Marine Technology.

facts.statement: Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus said on 8 February 2026 that forgery of skills training certificates and fraud are damaging the reputation of Bangladeshi workers in the international market, and ordered steps to stop it.

The National Skills Development Authority (NSDA, founded 2018) has started introducing a uniform-standard certification system across all training institutes, which the Chief Adviser said should help stop certificate forgery.

The NSDA governing body (second meeting, 8 February 2026; first was in 2022) decided to set up an integrated skills ecosystem so that training run by different ministries follows a common curriculum and standards, which it said would raise the value and credibility of certificates in the international market.

NSDA long-term goals approved on 8 February 2026 include skills gap analysis in emerging sectors, bringing all development projects under NSDA curricula and competency standards, aligning the Bangladesh National Qualifications Framework with international benchmarks, and bringing the large informal workforce under national skills certificates through 'recognition of prior learning'.
The meeting discussed issuing CDCs (continuous discharge certificates) to students trained at the Institutes of Marine Technology under the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment.

headline_en: Over 500 asylum seekers including Bangladeshis rescued from boat off Greek coast
summary_en: About 540 asylum seekers, including Bangladeshis, were rescued from a fishing boat south of Crete near Gavdos on Friday 19 December 2025 by a Frontex boat. They were taken to Rethymno, where asylum processing would begin after health checks. The article notes the EU's new migration and asylum pact takes effect next June and Greece's PM says rejected claimants will be returned.

facts.statement: At dawn on Friday 19 December 2025 a Frontex (EU border agency) boat patrolling near the small island of Gavdos in the Libyan Sea rescued about 540 asylum seekers from a fishing boat south of Crete; the boat's departure point was not immediately confirmed. Those rescued included nationals of Bangladesh, Pakistan, Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia, Sudan and Palestine.
facts.source_in_article: Greek coast guard spokesperson to AFP

facts.statement: The rescued asylum seekers were taken to Rethymno on Crete; their asylum application process was to begin after health checks.
facts.source_in_article: Greek coast guard spokesperson to AFP

facts.statement: On Thursday 18 December 2025 Frontex rescued 65 men and 5 women from two boats in distress off Gavdos.
Many asylum seekers travelling by sea to Europe used to depart from Libya; Crete and Gavdos are Greek islands in the Mediterranean, Gavdos lying south of Crete in the Libyan Sea.

The EU's new migration and asylum pact takes effect in June (2026), under which Greece, Cyprus, Spain and Italy will get help with migration pressure; Greek PM Kyriakos Mitsotakis said priority will be given to returning asylum seekers whose protection claims are rejected. Human rights groups warn the pact is risky for asylum seekers and may violate their rights.
facts.source_in_article: article; Kyriakos Mitsotakis; human rights groups
